question:
A 16-month-old boy with an unremarkable medical history is evaluated in the emergency department
for the second time within 5 days. His initial visit was due to rhinorrhea, fever, and cough, for which he
received nasal suctioning before being discharged. According to his mother, he has developed
increased respiratory rate and chest retractions over the past 5 days. Current vital signs show a
temperature of 100.7°F, respiratory rate of 44, and oxygen saturation of 90%. The physical
examination reveals tachypnea, expiratory wheezes, and hypoxia. Which of the following represents
the most appropriate treatment approach? Answer Choices: (A) Oral antibiotics, bronchodilators and
chest physiotherapy (B) Humidified oxygen, racemic epinephrine and intravenous (IV) dexamethasone
(C) Nasal suctioning, oxygen therapy and IV fluids (D) Intramuscular epinephrine, IV fluids and oxygen
therapy (E) High-flow nasal cannula, oral oseltamivir and IV antibiotics (F) IV cefotaxime and IV
vancomycin (G) Inhaled ipratropium bromide, oral azithromycin and IV fluids (H) Cool mist
humidification, oral decongestants and bronchodilators (I) Nebulized albuterol, oral corticosteroids and
antipyretics (J) Nebulized hypertonic saline, oral dexamethasone and oxygen therapy
 A. Inhaled ipratropium bromide, oral azithromycin and IV fluids
B. Nebulized albuterol, oral corticosteroids and antipyretics
C. Nasal suctioning, oxygen therapy and IV fluids
D. Nebulized hypertonic saline, oral dexamethasone and oxygen therapy
E. Humidified oxygen, racemic epinephrine and intravenous (IV) dexamethasone
F. Oral antibiotics, bronchodilators and chest physiotherapy
G. Intramuscular epinephrine, IV fluids and oxygen therapy
H. High-flow nasal cannula, oral oseltamivir and IV antibiotics

I. IV cefotaxime and IV vancomycin
J. Cool mist humidification, oral decongestants and bronchodilators
